title: MRC Laboratory of Molecular Biology antibody research → Cambridge Antibody Technology
summary: Monoclonal antibodies were invented at the UK Medical Research Council's Laboratory of Molecular Biology (LMB) in 1975 and were not patented after Britain's National Research Development Corporation declined. Later LMB antibody-engineering work by Greg Winter's group was patented: Cambridge Antibody Technology (CAT), founded around 1989–1990 by David Chiswell and MRC scientists including Winter, took an exclusive MRC license to phage-antibody library technology and paid the MRC royalties. CAT discovered the antibody that Abbott developed as Humira; after royalty litigation, Abbott paid $255 million in 2005 that CAT passed to the MRC and other licensors. AstraZeneca acquired CAT in 2006. LMB research continued.

links.claim: CAT's 20-F states it initially developed its technology in cooperation with the MRC and holds an exclusive license (agreement of January 7, 1997, subject to rights retained by the MRC) to MRC intellectual property on phage antibody libraries, including the Winter II, McCafferty and Griffiths patent families, paying the MRC 3% royalties on its own sales and 1%–2.3% on sub-licensees' sales.

links.claim: Under a 2005 settlement of the Humira royalty litigation, Abbott paid CAT $255 million, which CAT immediately paid to its licensors (the MRC, the Scripps Institute and Stratagene) in lieu of their royalties on Humira sales from January 1, 2005.

links.claim: CAT says it was established in 1990 by David Chiswell and leading MRC scientists. The Gairdner Foundation describes Greg Winter, a member of the MRC LMB who invented antibody humanization techniques in 1986, as a founder of CAT (1989); BioSpace reports his phage display technology was the company's foundation.

claims.claim: Britain gave away monoclonal antibodies by failing to patent them.
claims.explanation: The 1975 Köhler–Milstein hybridoma technique was not patented: the National Research Development Corporation said it could not identify immediate commercial applications. But later LMB antibody-engineering inventions were patented and licensed; History & Policy reports the MRC has earned more than £486 million in royalties from them, including through CAT.

claims.claim: Humira came out of publicly funded UK research.
claims.explanation: CAT, built on MRC-licensed phage antibody technology, isolated and optimized Humira's antibody in collaboration with Abbott, and the MRC was among the licensors paid in lieu of Humira royalties. Abbott, a private company, carried out its development and marketing.
